conventions: TypeScript strict; ESM; Prettier via @excalidraw/prettier-config (2-space indent, double quotes, trailing commas, 80-column wrap); the file_checks fix commands reformat, so never hand-align.
ESLint runs with --max-warnings=0; import/order groups are builtin, external, @excalidraw/** (after external), parent, sibling, then type-only imports last, each group separated by one blank line.
Type-only imports use a separate `import type { X } from "...";` statement (consistent-type-imports, separate-type-imports style).
Inside packages/excalidraw, import sibling modules relatively (`../types`, `./utils`); never import from the package barrel (`../index`) in source files (tests may, as lasso.test.tsx already does).
Helpers are `const` arrow functions; module-private helpers are not exported; prefer `const`, `?.` and `??`.

The lasso util runs on every pointer move: per candidate, Wrap mode runs at most the all-points enclosure test and, only for a fully enclosed candidate, the existing intersection test (today runs enclosure then intersection); extra allocation is limited to clamped points of frame children and one group pass that runs only when an enclosed element belongs to a group.

Tests run on Vitest with jsdom and globals (`describe`, `it`, `it.each`, `expect`, `beforeEach` are not imported); render with `render` from ./test-utils, drive state through `API` (./helpers/api) and `act`, assert selection with `assertSelectedElements` or `getSelectedElements`.
Do not add locale strings, UI controls, AppState fields or snapshot files; do not hand-edit __snapshots__.
Comments are short and only where the reason is not obvious from the code.

decisions.topic: Wrap ("contain") test in the lasso util
decisions.choice: An element qualifies in contain mode only when (1) every point of every one of its precomputed outline segments (elementsSegments), clamped into its frame clip bounds when it has them, lies inside the lasso polygon by polygonIncludesPointNonZero, and then (2) intersectionTest finds no lasso edge cutting the element (or, for a clipped frame child, no cut inside the clip bounds); intersectionTest runs only on candidates that pass (1).
rejected: Reuse the existing enclosureTest (any single outline point inside), which still selects an element whose corner the lasso clips
All-points enclosure without the intersection test, which selects an element a concave lasso notch cuts across (refused at Gate 2)
decisions.reason: NFR-2 puts correctness first and allows intersection on Wrap candidates; an element is enclosed only when all outline points are inside and no lasso edge crosses it, and per-candidate work stays within today's enclosure-then-intersection.

decisions.topic: Default when the mode input is omitted
decisions.choice: getLassoSelectedElementIds treats an omitted boxSelectionMode as "overlap"; LassoTrail always passes this.app.state.boxSelectionMode.
rejected: Default to "contain" like getElementsWithinSelection, which changes the result for existing direct callers
decisions.reason: AC-6 and NFR-1: callers that omit the input keep today's result.

decisions.choice: In contain mode a frame qualifies only when its own outline is fully enclosed (selectElementsFromIds then drops its children as today). A frame child is clipped as in elementsOverlappingBBox: when getContainingFrame(element, elementsMap) returns a frame and elementOverlapsWithFrame(element, frame, elementsMap) is true, clipBounds = getElementBounds(frame, elementsMap); its outline points are clamped into clipBounds (x into [clipBounds[0], clipBounds[2]], y into [clipBounds[1], clipBounds[3]]) before the polygon test, and an intersection hit counts only when pointInsideBounds(hit, clipBounds). A child that does not overlap its frame is tested unclipped.
rejected: Require a frame child's whole outline, including the part hidden outside the frame (refused at Gate 2)
Exact polygon clipping of the outline against the frame, which adds new geometry where clamping to the frame AABB mirrors box selection's AABB clip
decisions.reason: FR-6 (b) and A-2: box selection clips a child's bounds to its frame, so only the visible part has to be enclosed; the clip uses the same frame lookup and overlap test box selection uses.

decisions.topic: Bound text labels in Wrap mode (assumption A-3)
decisions.choice: In contain mode the util skips elements for which isBoundToContainer(element) is true, so a container qualifies only by its own outline; overlap mode keeps today's handling (labels tested and mapped to their container by selectElementsFromIds).
rejected: No bound-text rule (A-3 as written), under which a lasso enclosing only a label selects its unenclosed container in Wrap mode and breaks AC-1
decisions.reason: Mirrors box selection, whose shouldIgnoreElementFromSelection ignores bound text; recorded as A-3.

decisions.choice: After the loop, in contain mode only, the util drops every member of a failing top-level group from enclosedElements: a group (groupId = element.groupIds.at(-1)) fails when some member in elementsMap that is not deleted, not locked and not bound to a container is missing from enclosedElements. The pass runs only when at least one enclosed element has a groupId. Overlap mode keeps today's expansion by selectGroupsForSelectedElements.
rejected: Expand any qualifying member to its whole group in Wrap mode (refused at Gate 2)
Collect group members from the `elements` input, which in the app is the viewport-visible subset and would ignore off-screen members
decisions.reason: FR-6 (a): mirrors elementsOverlappingBBox's contain-mode group.every check over the top-level group, with locked and bound-text members ignored as shouldIgnoreElementFromSelection does; elementsMap holds all non-deleted elements, as box selection's scene elements do.

decisions.choice: `import type { BoxSelectionMode } from "../types";` in lasso/utils.ts and in tests/lasso.test.tsx; types.ts is not edited.
decisions.reason: The type already exists in packages/excalidraw/types.ts and is off-limits for edits.

decisions.choice: selectedElementIds stays [...intersectedElements, ...enclosedElements]; in contain mode intersectedElements stays empty.
decisions.reason: Keeps overlap output byte-identical to today.

decisions.choice: lasso.test.tsx's updatePath takes a required boxSelectionMode argument and every existing call passes "overlap"; selection.test.tsx's "lasso reselection" describe renders with initialData appState boxSelectionMode "overlap".
rejected: Rewrite those tests to assert the Wrap result, which turns their selections into empty assertions
decisions.reason: FR-7: the existing cases exercise intersection; pinning them keeps every assertion intact.

decisions.choice: packages/excalidraw/tests/__snapshots__/selection.test.tsx.snap is not edited: no new test uses snapshots and no existing snapshot test draws a lasso.
decisions.reason: Snapshots are regenerated only when one shifts.

decisions.choice: A new `### Behavior changes` heading with one bullet under `## Excalidraw Library` in the Unreleased block, after its `### Breaking changes` list, linking issue #11809.
decisions.reason: It is an editor behaviour change, not an API change; no PR number exists yet, so the issue is linked.

units.behaviour: getLassoSelectedElementIds takes an optional boxSelectionMode: "overlap" (or omitted) keeps today's enclosed-or-intersected result; "contain" mirrors box selection's contain mode: an element qualifies only when its (frame-clipped) outline is fully inside the lasso and no lasso edge cuts it, and a group qualifies only when every member qualifies.
rules: 1. Add `boxSelectionMode?: BoxSelectionMode;` as the last field of the input object type (after simplifyDistance) and destructure it as `boxSelectionMode = "overlap"`.

2. Keep the path simplification, the unlockedElements filter, the clearing of both sets, the lassoBounds reduce and the doBoundsIntersect / not-already-in-a-set guard exactly as they are, for both modes.
3. In the loop, when boxSelectionMode === "contain" and isBoundToContainer(element) is true, `continue` before the bounds guard.

4. Inside the guarded block, when boxSelectionMode === "contain": const frame = getContainingFrame(element, elementsMap); const clipBounds = frame && elementOverlapsWithFrame(element, frame, elementsMap) ? getElementBounds(frame, elementsMap) : null; add element.id to enclosedElements only when fullEnclosureTest(path, element, elementsSegments, clipBounds) is true and then intersectionTest(path, element, elementsMap, clipBounds) is false (call intersectionTest only after fullEnclosureTest passed). Never add to intersectedElements in this branch.
5. Otherwise (overlap) keep today's branch unchanged: enclosureTest first, then intersectionTest(path, element, elementsMap) only when not enclosed.

6. After the loop, when boxSelectionMode === "contain": collect the top-level group ids `elementsMap.get(id)?.groupIds.at(-1)` of the enclosed ids into a Set (skip undefined); when that Set is empty do nothing more. Otherwise mark a group as failing when some element of elementsMap.values() with !isDeleted, !locked and !isBoundToContainer has that top-level group id and is not in enclosedElements; then delete from enclosedElements every id whose element's groupIds.at(-1) is a failing group. Iterate a copy (`[...enclosedElements]`) when deleting.
7. Return { selectedElementIds: [...intersectedElements, ...enclosedElements] } as today.

8. Add a module-private `const fullEnclosureTest = (lassoPath: GlobalPoint[], element: ExcalidrawElement, elementsSegments: ElementsSegmentsMap, clipBounds: Bounds | null): boolean` placed right after enclosureTest: build the polygon once with polygonFromPoints(lassoPath); return false when the element has no segments entry or an empty one; otherwise return segments.every(segment => segment.every(point => polygonIncludesPointNonZero(p, lassoPolygon))) where p is the point itself when clipBounds is null, else pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(Math.min(Math.max(point[0], clipBounds[0]), clipBounds[2]), Math.min(Math.max(point[1], clipBounds[1]), clipBounds[3])).

9. intersectionTest gains a fourth parameter `clipBounds: Bounds | null = null`. When it is null the function body behaves exactly as today (onlyFirst true, `.length > 0`). When it is set, both intersectElementWithLineSegment calls (element and bound text) pass onlyFirst false and count as a hit only when the returned points `.some((point) => pointInsideBounds(point, clipBounds))` (pointInsideBounds(p, bounds: Bounds): boolean is the strict check exported by @excalidraw/element). Keep the lassoSegments construction and the bound-text positioning as they are.

10. Add `pointFrom` to the @excalidraw/math named import; add `elementOverlapsWithFrame`, `getContainingFrame`, `isBoundToContainer` and `pointInsideBounds` to the existing named import from "@excalidraw/element"; add `import type { BoxSelectionMode } from "../types";` as the last import, after a blank line.
11. Do not change enclosureTest.

units.behaviour: LassoTrail.updateSelection passes the current app state's boxSelectionMode into getLassoSelectedElementIds on every update.
rules: 1. Add `boxSelectionMode: this.app.state.boxSelectionMode,` as the last property of the object passed to getLassoSelectedElementIds, after simplifyDistance.
2. Read the state at call time (inside updateSelection); do not cache the mode on the instance.
3. Nothing else in the file changes: selectElementsFromIds, startPath, endPath and the shift/keepPreviousSelection handling stay as they are.

units.behaviour: Pins every existing lasso case to overlap mode and adds unit-level coverage of both modes for each shape kind, the omitted-mode default, bound-text labels, frames (including a child protruding from its frame), groups and a concave lasso cutting an element.
rules: 1. Imports: replace the `./test-utils` import line with `import { API } from "./helpers/api";`, a blank line, the unchanged `import { act, render } from "./test-utils";`, a blank line, and `import type { BoxSelectionMode } from "../types";` (type import last).

2. updatePath gains a required third parameter `boxSelectionMode: BoxSelectionMode`; its first statement is `API.setAppState({ boxSelectionMode });` (outside the existing act), and the direct getLassoSelectedElementIds call passes `boxSelectionMode` as its last field. Everything else in updatePath stays as it is.
3. Every existing `updatePath(startPoint, points);` call becomes `updatePath(startPoint, points, "overlap");`; no existing assertion changes.

4. Append one top-level `describe("lasso box selection mode", ...)` after the last describe. Its beforeEach sets the lasso tool inside act (`h.app.setActiveTool({ type: "lasso" })`); the file-level beforeEach already renders.

5. Inside it define `squareLasso = (x: number, y: number, size: number)` returning `{ startPoint: pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(x, y), points: [[0, 0], [size, 0], [size, size], [0, size], [0, 0]] as LocalPoint[] }`, and two constants: ENCLOSING = squareLasso(-50, -50, 200) and TOUCHING = squareLasso(60, 60, 200).

6. Define `shapes` as an array of `[label, () => ExcalidrawElement]` tuples, each factory calling API.createElement with a literal type: rectangle {x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100}; ellipse same box; diamond same box; "rotated rectangle" {type: "rectangle", x: 20, y: 20, width: 60, height: 60, angle: Math.PI / 4}; line {x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100, points: [pointFrom<LocalPoint>(0, 0), pointFrom<LocalPoint>(100, 100)]}; arrow with the same props; freedraw {x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100, points: [pointFrom<LocalPoint>(0, 0), pointFrom<LocalPoint>(50, 20), pointFrom<LocalPoint>(100, 100)]}.

7. Shape cases use it.each(shapes) with a `%s` title; each creates the element, calls API.setElements([element]), runs updatePath with the lasso's startPoint and points and the mode, and asserts the selected ids with getSelectedElements(h.elements, h.state).map(e => e.id).

8. The omitted-mode case calls getLassoSelectedElementIds directly (no updatePath): lassoPath is the TOUCHING square as five GlobalPoints (60,60), (260,60), (260,260), (60,260), (60,60); elementsSegments is built with getElementLineSegments over h.elements as updatePath does; fresh Sets are passed on every call.

9. The bound-text case uses API.createTextContainer(), API.setElements on both returned elements, reads the label from the scene with API.getElement(label), and lassos a square from (label.x - 5, label.y - 5) with size Math.max(label.width, label.height) + 10.

10. The frame cases create a frame with API.createElement({ type: "frame", x: 0, y: 0, width: 400, height: 400 }) and a child rectangle {x: 50, y: 50, width: 100, height: 100, frameId: frame.id}; the child-only lasso is squareLasso(25, 25, 150) and the whole-frame lasso is squareLasso(-50, -50, 500).

11. The protruding-child case creates a frame {type: "frame", x: 0, y: 0, width: 200, height: 200} and a child rectangle {x: 150, y: 50, width: 100, height: 100, frameId: frame.id} (its right half lies outside the frame), and lassos the visible part with startPoint pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(140, 40) and points [[0, 0], [70, 0], [70, 120], [0, 120], [0, 0]] as LocalPoint[].

12. The group cases create rectA {type: "rectangle", x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100, groupIds: ["g1"]} and rectB the same at x: 300; the one-member lasso is ENCLOSING (encloses rectA only) and the whole-group lasso is squareLasso(-50, -50, 500).

13. The concave case creates a rectangle {x: 0, y: 0, width: 100, height: 100} and a lasso with startPoint pointFrom<GlobalPoint>(-50, -50) and points [[0, 0], [90, 0], [100, 100], [110, 0], [200, 0], [200, 200], [0, 200], [0, 0]] as LocalPoint[]: all four corners lie inside the polygon while the notch reaching (50, 50) cuts the rectangle's top edge.

units.behaviour: Pins the existing lasso reselection test to overlap mode and adds UI-level lasso tests driven by the mouse in Wrap and Overlap mode, including a partially touched element and a mid-session preference change.
rules: 1. The "lasso reselection" beforeEach renders `<Excalidraw initialData={{ appState: { boxSelectionMode: "overlap" } }} />` instead of `<Excalidraw />`; its test body is unchanged.

2. Add a top-level `describe("lasso box selection mode", ...)` right after the "lasso reselection" describe. Inside it define `lassoSelect = (points: [number, number][])`: act(() => h.app.setActiveTool({ type: "lasso" })), mouse.downAt on the first point, mouse.moveTo on each remaining point, then mouse.up().

3. Scene for every case: rect1 = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 0, y: 0, width: 50, height: 50, backgroundColor: "red", fillStyle: "solid" }) and rect2 the same at x: 100; API.setElements([rect1, rect2]).
4. The lasso for every case is lassoSelect([[-20, -20], [125, -20], [125, 70], [-20, 70], [-20, -20]]): rect1 is fully enclosed, rect2 is only partially covered.

5. Use two nested describes: "wrap (contain)" whose beforeEach renders with initialData appState boxSelectionMode "contain", and "overlap" whose beforeEach renders with boxSelectionMode "overlap"; render is awaited as in the box-selection overlap mode describe.
6. The preference-change case lives in the wrap describe and calls API.setAppState({ boxSelectionMode: "overlap" }) before lassoSelect.
7. Assert with assertSelectedElements; no snapshots.

units.behaviour: Records under Unreleased that the lasso now honours the Wrap/Overlap box selection preference and that the default (Wrap) lasso is enclose-only.
rules: 1. Insert, after the last Breaking changes bullet of the Unreleased `## Excalidraw Library` section: a blank line, `### Behavior changes`, a blank line, and one bullet.

2. The bullet says: the lasso tool now follows the box selection mode preference (`appState.boxSelectionMode`); in the default Wrap (`"contain"`) mode it selects only elements it fully encloses, matching box selection (a group only when all its members are enclosed, a frame child by its part visible inside the frame), while Overlap (`"overlap"`) mode keeps the previous behavior of also selecting elements the lasso path touches; it ends with `[#11809](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/11809)`.

3. Mention that `getLassoSelectedElementIds` is unaffected for callers that omit the new optional `boxSelectionMode` input only if it fits in the same bullet as one short clause; add no other bullets.
